---
title: "Handling density dependent parameter values"
---
# Handling density dependent parameter values

Parameter values that depend on previous population abundance or biomass values can be incorporated 
by treating the population quantity as an environmental time series and updating that time series 
on a by-season basis: 

  * $N(y,s)$ gets calculated
  * $e_j(y,s) = f(N(y,s))$ converts $N$ to the desired population quantity, where $f$ is the function that converts $N$ to $e$

For a parameter value $p_{F}(f,y,s,d)$, the arithmetic ($p^a_{F}(f,y,s,d)$) and transform-scale ($p^t_{F}(f,y,s,d)$) components can then be calculated as 

$$ p^a(y,s) = \bar {p}^a(y,s) + \{\sum_{i} \epsilon^a_{i}(f,d) \cdot \rho^a_{i}(f,d) \cdot e_{j(i)}(y-k(i),s-l(i))\}$$
